set.body:
Objective:
Add the high-value logical optimizer and capability-driven source/sink boundary without allowing physical backends to redefine Frame semantics.

Optimizer scope:
- Projection pruning through filters, aggregates, joins, sorts, windows, and nested projections.
- Predicate composition and source pushdown only where SourceCapabilities prove support.
- Null- and floating-aware expression simplification.
- Filter/projection fusion, limit pushdown, and redundant projection elimination.
- Every rewrite is explainable and tested for semantic equivalence by executing original and optimized plans over generated batches.

Source and sink protocol:
- Sources expose schema inspection separately from lazy data scanning.
- Scan requests carry column selection, portable predicate, limit, and batch-size hints.
- Capabilities describe projection, predicate, limit, partition, statistics, and streaming support.
- Plans hold immutable source descriptions; execution scopes open and close readers.
- Sinks consume batch streams and return structured receipts.

Baseline adapters:
- In-memory record batches.
- CSV with explicit inference/coercion policy.
- Arrow IPC on the platforms where a conforming adapter exists; cross-platform fixtures establish equivalent schemas and values.
- Parquet and database adapters remain separate beads and must use the same capability protocol.

Acceptance:
- Optimizer-equivalence laws cover nulls, NaNs, chunks, aliases, and join/aggregate dependencies.
- A pushed-down scan reads only required columns and demonstrates early termination when supported.
- Unsupported pushdown remains above the source rather than disappearing.
- Schema inspection errors, source failures, write failures, and allocation failures are structured ADTs.
- Explain output shows requested, accepted, and residual pushdown plus allocation/copy receipts.
set.title: Frame foundation 5: lawful optimizer and capability-driven sources, sinks, CSV, and Arrow IPC
